answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The garden multiplier is published, charged in shale, and onyx lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1035 identities would post 3652 proofs and burn roughly 32 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
